answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, each new agent must lock a bond priced in a scarce credit called saffron, minted only from verified useful labor, not self-issued claims. Credits vest on a shale schedule: the lock cannot be withdrawn or used to vote until two settlement cycles pass, and later proof of key reuse slashes the bond. A public tide of peer attestations can freeze suspicious clusters mid-vesting. An attacker who wants many identities must prepay scarce credits, wait through delayed vesting, and risk losing every lock at once, swamping the payoff from stuffed ballots.
